subject: Serrano Health — sudden p99 & errors after quant profile swap
messages:
From: Alex Martin <alex.martin@serranohealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Serrano Health Support <support@serranohealth.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Urgent: p99 spike + error rate after your v4.2 quant swap

Irene —

We just saw a large regression starting ~03:05 UTC after you rolled the v4.2 quant profile for our tenant. p99 has jumped from ~220ms to ~1.4s for the primary route, and we’re also seeing a 3.2% 5xx spike (previously <0.1%). This is impacting our triage pipelines — retries are compounding the load.

We reported during the maintenance window but this was supposed to be safe. Can you confirm whether Serrano was included in the quant rollout and what immediate mitigations you can apply? We need either a rollback or a safe routing to the older flavor — this is customer-facing.

I’m attaching a trace and a small CSV with sample request ids. We’re on a tight compliance window and cannot sustain higher tail latencies.

—Alex
Alex Martin
Lead SRE, Serrano Health

Attachments: serrano_p99_trace_1111.zip (zip), perf_dump_1111.csv (csv)
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martin <alex.martin@serranohealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Urgent: p99 spike + error rate after your v4.2 quant swap

Alex — thanks for the quick flag and for the traces. I’m looping in Jonas and Marcus from the inference runtime team and Priyom from customer success. We’ll take this to an incident bridge right now.

Immediate asks from our side: can you confirm the last 6 request IDs in the CSV that had 5xx so we can map to backend logs? We’ll start with one of two mitigations:

- Fast route cut: move Serrano traffic to the v4.1 fp16 variant (no quant) while we investigate. This will increase cost but should restore latency.
- Scoped rollback: revert the v4.2 quant profile for Serrano tenant only.

We’ll propose the fastest path in the bridge. ETA for a remediation decision: 20 minutes.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Account Engineering, Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Alex Martin <alex.martin@serranohealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:40:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Urgent: p99 spike + error rate after your v4.2 quant swap

Alex / team — quick snapshot from the runtime: we see a correlated increase in KV cache misses for Serrano’s shard coincident with the quant profile flip at 03:03:48 UTC. Two likely hypotheses so far:

1) Quantized kernel path change: the v4.2 quant profile enables a fused attention kernel with different tokenization padding behavior in edge cases. For long-context requests we’re hitting more expensive attention loops (unexpected runtime path) which increases decode time.
2) Beam-search divergence + repeat penalties interacting poorly with quantized logits: some inputs now produce longer decode due to subword boundary sensitivity after quantization, which increases average tokens-per-request and thus p99.

We’re starting a scoped revert for Serrano (tenant routing update to v4.1-fp16) now — this should be a quick route swap (no model weight re-deploy). If the revert completes cleanly we’ll monitor for 30 minutes and confirm.

Action items we’ll take immediately:
- Route swap to v4.1-fp16 for Serrano (in progress).
- Capture end-to-end traces and the decoding logs for the sample request ids Alex provided.
- Postmortem with quant profile telemetry to follow.

Jonas
Senior Software Engineer, Inference Runtime
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Alex Martin <alex.martin@serranohealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 10:02:45 -0800
Subject: Re: Urgent: Serrano p99 + errors — route swap in place

Update — we flipped Serrano to v4.1-fp16 at 09:58:18 PST (routing change pushed). Early signals:
- p99 for the primary route dropped from ~1.4s to ~240ms within two minutes.
- 5xx rate is back under 0.2% and trending down.

We’re keeping a hot fallback in place (v4.1) + temporary autoscale bump for the tenant for the next 2 hours to absorb retry-induced load. Marcus monitoring dashboards: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cSerranoLogs

Next steps proposed:
- Incident window: 2 hours of stabilized traffic, then a controlled canary re-deploy of a modified quant profile that removes the fused attention optimization for long-context requests.
- Postmortem and customer-facing summary within 24 hours.

Marcus Lin
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martin <alex.martin@serranohealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 17:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Serrano incident — mitigation complete and exec note

Alex —

Thanks again for the rapid report and the traces. Summary of what happened and our commitments:

What we saw: after the v4.2 quant profile rollout a specific fused attention kernel path triggered for a subset of Serrano inputs which increased decode time and caused higher 5xxs as retries piled up.

What we did:
- Immediate tenant routing rollback to v4.1-fp16 completed at 09:58 PST, p99 and 5xxs recovered.
- Temporary autoscale bump applied to absorb retry traffic.
- Engineering patch: we’ll ship a modified v4.2 quant (v4.2.1) that disables the long-context fused attention path and run a canary tonight on non-customer tenants.

Customer impact: transient degradation for ~55 minutes; no data loss and no PII exposure.

Compensation: Priyom will coordinate a one-month service credit for Serrano given SLA impact. Priyom — can you own outreach and confirm the credit amount?

Follow-ups: postmortem and detailed telemetry export (including decoded token histograms and kernel traces) within 24 hours. We’ll share the action items and schedule a technical review with Serrano engineering to validate the v4.2.1 canary before any further rollouts.

If you need an exec-to-exec note for your leadership, I can provide a concise summary.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Account Engineering, Redwood Inference

Priyom Das will follow up on credits and scheduling.
